name: Leading Change with Emotion — Hanseatic Naturkost
description: A four-round, intermediate change-leadership simulation set inside Hanseatic Naturkost GmbH, a EUR 480M Hamburg organic-food manufacturer (1,900 employees, 2 sites) that publicly committed to a 42% Scope 1&2 emissions cut by 2030 — and just missed its first milestone (3% achieved vs 6% needed). The science is solved; the people are not. A pulse survey shows the classic value-action gap: 71% of employees say they care about sustainability, yet only 22% have changed any work behavior. Worse, a leaked memo about "efficiency measures" has 48% of production staff reading decarbonization as code for automation and layoffs, 34% are guilt-fatigued and have tuned climate messaging out, and two of three works-council reps are skeptical. Playing the sustainability lead, you have EUR 600,000 and one quarter to lift the behavior-change rate from 22% toward a board target of 50% participation — without re-triggering anxiety. Grounded in Myriam Bechtoldt's research on discrete emotions in climate-mitigation behavior, the simulation runs four decisions: (1) diagnose the emotional landscape, mapping which discrete emotion — fear, guilt-fatigue, apathy, hope, pride — is blocking which segment, and distinguishing the value-action gap from outright opposition; (2) choose a communication frame — fear/urgency, guilt, hope/efficacy, or pride/identity — pricing each frame's effect on the message-effectiveness index per segment and naming its emotional risk, because fear and guilt spike attention but deepen avoidance while hope and efficacy build durable engagement; (3) manage an anxious town-hall and works-council, choosing emotion-regulation moves — validate before reframe, reframe threat as agency, offer credible rather than hollow job-security reassurance, give people control through choice; and (4) design the EUR 600,000 engagement initiative across peer champions, visible quick-wins, gamified challenges, recognition, manager-led conversations, and a transparent progress dashboard, building for persistence rather than a one-off spike. The math rewards matching frame to emotion, validating before reframing, credible reassurance, and a feedback-loop-backed engagement design — and punishes the five classic errors: treating it as an information deficit, defaulting to fear/guilt, answering feelings with spreadsheets, hollow over-promising on job security, and buying a one-off participation spike with no mechanism to make behavior stick. Final KPIs track Behavior-Change Rate (%), Emotion-Regulation Score, Message Effectiveness, and Resistance Risk.
view:
5 March 2026 · Hanseatic Naturkost GmbH, Hamburg · One quarter to lift behavior change from 22% to 50%

Leading Change with Emotion

You are the Head of Sustainability at a EUR 480M organic-food maker. The 2030 target is public, the first milestone was missed, and a memo about “efficiency measures” has leaked onto the packing floor. 71% say they care; 22% have changed how they work. You have 600.000 € and one quarter before the board review.

Round 1 of 4 One quarter to the board review

🌱
Round 1 — Diagnose

Your Decisions This Round

Campaign volume: 50%
0 is a restrained campaign; 100 is the loudest Hanseatic has ever spoken. What volume does depends on the frame it carries.
Share of each answer given to what people feel: 50
0 keeps every answer to the facts; 100 gives most of each answer to what people feel before turning to the facts.
Engagement budget allocated: 600 / 600 (thousand €)
How the workforce and the works council took it
The pulse survey gives you two lines that do not agree: 71% of the 1,900 employees say they care about sustainability, and 22% have changed anything about how they work. The rate came in at 21% and 22% in the two preceding cycles, with an information campaign running throughout. Each decision is made before you can see how the one before it landed. After each round, this panel tells you how the workforce and the works council took it.

Round-by-Round Record

Behavior Change, Regulation & Resistance Trajectory

text.en: Diagnose the gap between what a workforce says it values and what it does, and distinguish unmanaged fear from settled opposition segment by segment
text.es: Diagnosticar la brecha entre lo que una plantilla dice valorar y lo que hace, y distinguir, segmento a segmento, el miedo no gestionado de la oposición asentada

text.en: Regulate emotion in a live, adversarial room by validating before reframing, and distinguish credible reassurance from a guarantee that cannot be honoured
text.es: Regular la emoción en una sala hostil validando antes de reencuadrar, y distinguir una tranquilización creíble de una garantía que no se puede cumplir

text.en: Select a communication frame against the emotion each segment reports, calibrate its intensity, and state the risk the chosen frame carries
text.es: Seleccionar un enfoque de comunicación según la emoción que declara cada segmento, calibrar su intensidad y señalar el riesgo que conlleva el enfoque elegido

text.en: Design an engagement portfolio that survives the end of its own funding, and defend the allocation against a cheaper option that buys a participation spike
text.es: Diseñar una cartera de iniciativas de implicación que sobreviva al fin de su propia financiación, y defender el reparto frente a una opción más barata que compra un pico de participación

text.en: Evaluate a change programme on more than its headline participation number, and specify what else a board should see
text.es: Evaluar un programa de cambio por algo más que su cifra principal de participación, y especificar qué más debería ver un consejo

name.en: Reading the gap as an information deficit
name.es: Leer la brecha como un déficit de información

lure.en: With 71% saying they care, more facts and a business case look like the missing input, and it is the plan a communications budget already knows how to run
lure.es: Con un 71% que dice preocuparse, más datos y un caso de negocio parecen lo que falta, y es el plan que un presupuesto de comunicación ya sabe ejecutar

consequence.en: The frame is built for people who already agree: message effectiveness stays low, resistance rises, and every euro of the engagement budget returns less behaviour in Round 4
consequence.es: El marco se construye para quienes ya están de acuerdo: la eficacia del mensaje se queda baja, la resistencia sube y cada euro del presupuesto rinde menos cambio de conducta en la ronda 4

source.ref: TN §13 Student pitfalls, The information reflex; §7 Q1; §5.2

name.en: Urgency as the headline frame, with volume treated as a separate dial
name.es: La urgencia como marco principal, con el volumen tratado como un dial aparte

lure.en: Urgency is accurate and it gets attention at once; turning the volume up looks like the same message, only louder
lure.es: La urgencia es cierta y capta atención de inmediato; subir el volumen parece el mismo mensaje, solo que más alto

consequence.en: On a workforce that already reports a threat, a louder threat frame moves the most anxious group to avoidance: message effectiveness falls and resistance climbs with intensity, and the cost is paid in Rounds 3 and 4
consequence.es: En una plantilla que ya declara una amenaza, un marco de amenaza más alto lleva al grupo más ansioso a la evitación: la eficacia del mensaje cae y la resistencia sube con la intensidad, y el coste se paga en las rondas 3 y 4

source.ref: TN §13 Student pitfalls, Treating volume as separate from frame; §7 Q3; §5.3

name.en: Answering a feeling with a fact
name.es: Responder a un sentimiento con un dato

lure.en: The roadmap and the emissions data are true and to hand, and replying with them does not feel like a mistake to the person doing it
lure.es: La hoja de ruta y los datos de emisiones son ciertos y están a mano, y responder con ellos no le parece un error a quien lo hace

consequence.en: The fear leaves the room without leaving the workforce: emotion regulation drops, resistance rises through the works council, and the Round 4 money buys less
consequence.es: El miedo sale de la sala pero no de la plantilla: la regulación emocional baja, la resistencia sube a través del comité de empresa y el dinero de la ronda 4 compra menos

source.ref: TN §13 Student pitfalls, Answering a feeling with a fact; §7 Q2; §11 takeaway 2

lure.en: The room goes quiet and the regulation score rises the moment the guarantee is given
lure.es: La sala se calma y la regulación emocional sube en el momento en que se da la garantía

consequence.en: The promise is not hers to make and cannot be withdrawn: credibility is lost for the rest of the quarter, later messages are discounted, and the run cannot earn the top grade
consequence.es: La promesa no le corresponde y no puede retirarse: la credibilidad se pierde para el resto del trimestre, los mensajes posteriores se descuentan y la partida no puede alcanzar la máxima calificación

source.ref: TN §13 Student pitfalls, The comfortable guarantee; §7 Q2; §5.4; §9.1 run B

name.es: Comprar la semana de la encuesta

lure.en: The board target is a participation number measured by survey at one date; a leaderboard, prizes and a loud fortnight can reach it
lure.es: El objetivo del consejo es una cifra de participación medida por encuesta en una fecha; una clasificación, premios y dos semanas ruidosas pueden alcanzarla

consequence.en: Participation is bought, not built: the behaviour gain is cut, nothing keeps running after the budget ends, and the grade names a spike instead of a habit
consequence.es: La participación se compra, no se construye: la ganancia de conducta se recorta, nada sigue funcionando al acabar el presupuesto y la calificación nombra un pico en lugar de un hábito

source.ref: TN §13 Student pitfalls, Buying the survey week; §7 Q4; §5.6; §9.1 run C
